sketch_steps: derive: Expand both hypotheses bilinearly.
derive: Subtracting the first from the second gives c·d + a·b - b·d - a·c = 0.
conclude: That expression equals (d - a)·(c - b).

sketch_steps: setup: Let x = a+b-c, y = b+c-a, z = c+a-b.
derive: Pairwise sums are 2a, 2b, 2c, so at most one of x, y, z is nonpositive.
case_split: If one is nonpositive, the left side is at most 0.
apply_theorem: Otherwise AM-GM gives xy ≤ b², yz ≤ c², zx ≤ a².
conclude: Multiplying gives xyz ≤ abc.

sketch_steps: derive: A, B, C lie in [0, π], where sin is concave.
apply_theorem: Jensen's inequality with equal weights.
derive: The mean angle is π/3, and sin(π/3) = √3/2.
conclude: Multiplying by 3 gives the bound.

drafts.proof_strategy: Count the complement by inclusion-exclusion on non-divisibility by 2 and by 3.
sketch_steps: translate: The product is not divisible by 6 exactly when it is odd or not divisible by 3.
derive: An odd product means all faces lie in {1,3,5}, giving 3^n outcomes.
derive: A product prime to 3 means all faces lie in {1,2,4,5}, giving 4^n outcomes.
derive: Both conditions mean all faces lie in {1,5}, giving 2^n outcomes.
apply_theorem: Inclusion-exclusion gives 3^n + 4^n - 2^n outcomes in the complement.
conclude: Subtract from 6^n.

drafts.canonical_statement: A point starts at a vertex of a triangle and at each step moves to one of the other two vertices with probability 1/2, independently. With the vertices as residues mod 3, each step +1 or +2, and all 2^n step sequences equally likely, the probability of being at the start after n steps equals 1/3 + (2/3)(-1/2)^n.

drafts.proof_strategy: Condition on the position after n steps to get a recurrence, then shift by the fixed point 1/3 to obtain a geometric sequence.
sketch_steps: setup: Encode vertices mod 3 and steps as +1 or +2, with all 2^n step sequences equally likely.
translate: Conditioning on the position after n steps gives p_{n+1} = (1 - p_n)/2 with p_0 = 1.
derive: Subtracting the fixed point gives p_{n+1} - 1/3 = (-1/2)(p_n - 1/3).
induction: The shifted sequence is geometric with first term 2/3.

drafts.canonical_statement: Tower law: for fields F ⊂ K ⊂ L with [K:F] and [L:K] finite, L/F is finite and [L:F] = [L:K][K:F].

drafts.proof_strategy: Multiply a basis of K/F by a basis of L/K and show the products form a basis of L/F.
sketch_steps: setup: Choose a basis a_i of K over F and a basis b_j of L over K.
derive: Expanding coefficients shows that the products a_i b_j span L over F.
derive: Linear independence of b_j and then of a_i shows that the products are independent over F.
conclude: Counting the basis gives [L:F] = [K:F][L:K], so L/F is finite.

drafts.canonical_statement: If E/F is a finite extension and x ∈ E, then the degree of the minimal polynomial of x over F divides [E:F].
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dvd"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimal_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ext_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the tower law to F ⊂ F(x) ⊂ E and identify [F(x):F] with the degree of the minimal polynomial.
sketch_steps: translate: Since E/F is finite, x is algebraic and [F(x):F] equals the degree of its minimal polynomial.
apply_theorem: The tower law gives [E:F] = [E:F(x)][F(x):F].
conclude: Therefore the degree of the minimal polynomial divides [E:F].

drafts.canonical_statement: If x is algebraic over a field F, then its minimal polynomial over F is irreducible over F.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="field_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimal_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Factor the minimal polynomial and use that E has no zero divisors together with minimality of the degree.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose the minimal polynomial m factors as g h.
derive: Evaluating at x gives g(x)h(x) = 0, so one factor vanishes at x.
derive: Minimality of deg m forces the other factor to be constant.
conclude: Since deg m ≥ 1, m is irreducible.

drafts.canonical_statement: If x is algebraic over a field F and f in F[X] satisfies f(x) = 0, then the minimal polynomial of x over F divides f.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="field_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_eval"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="dvd"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimal_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Divide f by the minimal polynomial and use minimality of the degree on the remainder.
sketch_steps: setup: Write f = q m + r with deg r < deg m.
derive: Evaluating at x gives r(x) = 0.
contradiction: A nonzero r would contradict minimality of deg m.
conclude: Hence r = 0 and m divides f.

drafts.canonical_statement: A monic irreducible polynomial over F having x as a root equals the minimal polynomial of x over F.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="field_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="monic_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_eval"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimal_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The minimal polynomial divides p, and irreducibility plus monicity force equality.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Since p(x) = 0, the minimal polynomial m divides p.
derive: Irreducibility of p and non-constancy of m give p = c m with c a nonzero constant.
conclude: Comparing leading coefficients of monic polynomials gives c = 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: If x is algebraic over a field F, then [F(x):F] equals the degree of the minimal polynomial of x over F.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="field_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ext_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimal_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show 1, x, ..., x^(n-1) is a basis of F(x) using division by the minimal polynomial.
sketch_steps: setup: Let m be the minimal polynomial of x and n its degree.
derive: The evaluation map has kernel (m), and irreducibility of m gives F(x) = F[x].
derive: Division by m shows that 1, x, ..., x^(n-1) span F(x).
derive: Minimality of n shows that these powers are linearly independent.
conclude: Thus [F(x):F] = n.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every finite extension of fields is algebraic.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Powers of x are linearly dependent in a finite-dimensional space, which gives an annihilating polynomial.
sketch_steps: setup: Let n = [E:F] and fix x in E.
derive: The n+1 elements 1, x, ..., x^n are linearly dependent over F.
conclude: A nontrivial relation is a nonzero polynomial with root x, so x is algebraic.

drafts.canonical_statement: If x and y are algebraic over a field F, then x+y, xy and -x are algebraic over F, and x⁻¹ is algebraic over F whenever x ≠ 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: All four elements lie in F(x,y), which is finite over F by the tower law.
sketch_steps: derive: F(x)/F is finite because x is algebraic, and F(x,y)/F(x) is finite because y is algebraic.
apply_theorem: The tower law shows that F(x,y)/F is finite.
translate: The elements x+y, xy, -x and x⁻¹ all lie in F(x,y).
conclude: Elements of a finite extension are algebraic.

drafts.canonical_statement: If K/F and L/K are algebraic extensions, then L/F is algebraic.

drafts.proof_strategy: Pass to the finite subextension generated by the coefficients of a polynomial annihilating x.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix x in L and a polynomial over K with root x.
construct: Let K_0 be the field generated over F by its coefficients.
derive: K_0/F is finite since the coefficients are algebraic, and K_0(x)/K_0 is finite.
apply_theorem: The tower law shows that K_0(x)/F is finite.
conclude: Hence x is algebraic over F.

drafts.canonical_statement: If f is irreducible over a field F, then in the field F[X]/(f) the class of X is a root of f, and the degree of this extension equals deg f.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="field_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="adjoin_root"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_eval"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="adjoin_root_generator"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ext_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="adjoin_root"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use that (f) is maximal, then count a basis of the quotient by division with remainder.
sketch_steps: translate: Since F[X] is a PID and f is irreducible, (f) is maximal and the quotient is a field.
derive: The class α of X satisfies f(α) = 0 because f maps to zero in the quotient.
derive: Division with remainder gives a unique representative of degree below n = deg f.
conclude: Thus 1, α, ..., α^(n-1) is a basis and the degree is n.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every polynomial f over a field F has a splitting field, and any two splitting fields of f are isomorphic over F.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="splitting_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="splitting_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="splitting_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="isomorphic_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Adjoin roots one irreducible factor at a time for existence, and extend isomorphisms root by root for uniqueness.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on deg f, for existence, by adjoining a root of an irreducible factor.
derive: The polynomial then has a linear factor, and the remaining factor has smaller degree.
induction: For uniqueness, prove more generally that an isomorphism of base fields extends to splitting fields.
construct: An isomorphism σ extends to F(α) ≅ F'(β) by sending a root α of g to a root β of σg.
conclude: Repeating this yields an F-isomorphism between any two splitting fields.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every field F has an algebraic closure, and any two algebraic closures of F are isomorphic over F.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_closure_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_closure_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_closure_of"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="isomorphic_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Build the closure by adjoining roots of all polynomials with Zorn-style maximal ideals, and compare closures through a maximal embedding.
sketch_steps: construct: Adjoin an indeterminate per monic polynomial and quotient by a maximal ideal containing the relations.
derive: Iterate and take the union to obtain an algebraically closed extension.
construct: The algebraic elements in this extension form an algebraic closure.
apply_theorem: Zorn's lemma extends the inclusion of F to an embedding of L into M.
derive: The image is algebraically closed and M/F is algebraic, so the embedding is surjective.
conclude: Any two algebraic closures are F-isomorphic.

drafts.canonical_statement: If k is algebraically closed and E/k is algebraic, then the canonical map k → E is surjective.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraically_closed"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: An irreducible polynomial over an algebraically closed field is linear, so the minimal polynomial of x has its root in k.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix x in E and let m be its minimal polynomial over k.
derive: Irreducible polynomials over k have degree 1, so m = X - a.
conclude: Then x = a lies in the image of k.

drafts.canonical_statement: A splitting field of a polynomial over a field F is a normal extension of F.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="splitting_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normal_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Compare the degrees of E over F(α) and E(β) over F(β), both splitting fields of f.
sketch_steps: setup: Take an irreducible g over F with roots α in E and β in an extension.
construct: There is an F-isomorphism F(α) ≅ F(β).
apply_theorem: E and E(β) are splitting fields of f over F(α) and F(β), so the isomorphism extends and the degrees agree.
derive: The tower law gives [E(β):F] = [E:F], hence β lies in E.
conclude: Thus g splits in E and E/F is normal.

drafts.canonical_statement: An irreducible polynomial f over a field F is separable if and only if its formal derivative f' is nonzero.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="separable_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_derivative"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Compare gcd(f, f') with the irreducible f using the degree of f'.
sketch_steps: translate: Separability means that f and f' are coprime.
case_split: If f' = 0, then gcd(f, f') = f is not constant, so f is not separable.
case_split: If f' is nonzero, its degree is below deg f, so irreducible f does not divide it.
conclude: Hence gcd(f, f') is constant and f is separable.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every field of characteristic zero and every finite field is perfect.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="or"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="field_characteristic"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="perfect_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show the derivative of an irreducible polynomial is nonzero, using surjectivity of Frobenius in the finite case.
sketch_steps: case_split: In characteristic zero, a nonconstant polynomial has a nonzero derivative.
case_split: In a finite field of characteristic p, the injective Frobenius map is surjective.
contradiction: If f' = 0 then f = g(X^p), and taking p-th roots of coefficients makes f a p-th power.
conclude: So irreducible polynomials have nonzero derivative and are separable.

drafts.canonical_statement: Every algebraic extension of a perfect field is separable.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="perfect_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraic_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="separable_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The minimal polynomial of each element is irreducible, hence separable over a perfect field.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix x in E and let m be its minimal polynomial over F.
derive: The polynomial m is irreducible over F.
apply_theorem: Irreducible polynomials over a perfect field are separable.
conclude: Every element of E is separable over F.

drafts.canonical_statement: A field K of prime characteristic p is perfect if and only if every element of K has a p-th root in K.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="P"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="field_characteristic"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="perfect_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use X^p - a as an inseparable irreducible polynomial for one direction, and take p-th roots of coefficients for the other.
sketch_steps: contradiction: If a has no p-th root, then X^p - a is irreducible with zero derivative, so K is not perfect.
setup: Conversely assume that every element has a p-th root and let f be irreducible with f' = 0.
derive: Then f = g(X^p) for some polynomial g.
derive: Taking p-th roots of the coefficients of g writes f as a p-th power.
conclude: This contradicts irreducibility, so every irreducible polynomial is separable.

drafts.canonical_statement: Primitive element theorem: a finite separable extension E/F is simple, that is, E = F(α) for some α in E.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="separable_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="simple_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Handle finite fields by a generator of the unit group, and reduce the infinite case to two generators with a generic linear combination.
sketch_steps: case_split: If F is finite, then a generator of the cyclic group of units of E is primitive.
translate: If F is infinite, reduce by induction to E = F(a, b).
construct: Choose c in F avoiding finitely many values so that α = a + c b separates the conjugate sums.
derive: Then gcd(g(α - cX), h(X)) = X - b, using that h has simple roots.
conclude: Thus b and then a lie in F(α), so E = F(α).

drafts.canonical_statement: For a prime p and a positive integer n, a field of order p^n exists, and any two fields of order p^n are isomorphic as rings.

drafts.proof_strategy: Construct the field as the root set of X^q - X and recognize every field of order q as its splitting field.
sketch_steps: construct: Let L be a splitting field of X^q - X over F_p, where q = p^n.
derive: The derivative is -1, so the roots are distinct and form a subfield of order q.
derive: In a field K of order q, every element satisfies x^q = x by Lagrange.
translate: Hence K is also a splitting field of X^q - X over its prime field.
apply_theorem: Uniqueness of splitting fields gives K ≅ L.

drafts.canonical_statement: The multiplicative group of a finite field is cyclic.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="cyclic_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="units_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Count elements of each order using that X^d - 1 has at most d roots and compare with the totient sum.
sketch_steps: setup: Let N be the order of the unit group and ψ(d) the number of elements of order d.
derive: Since X^d - 1 has at most d roots, ψ(d) is 0 or φ(d).
derive: The identities Σψ(d) = N = Σφ(d) force ψ(d) = φ(d) for each divisor d.
conclude: So ψ(N) is at least one, and a generator exists.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a finite extension L/K of a finite field K, the map x ↦ x^|K| is a K-automorphism of L of order [L:K], and it generates Gal(L/K).

drafts.proof_strategy: Compute the order of φ by counting roots of X^(q^i) - X and compare it with the bound on the number of automorphisms.
sketch_steps: setup: Let q = |K|, n = [L:K] and φ(x) = x^q.
derive: The map φ is a bijective ring map fixing K because x^q = x on K.
derive: Every element of L satisfies x^(q^n) = x, so φ^n = id.
contradiction: If φ^i = id with i < n, then X^(q^i) - X would have more roots than its degree.
apply_theorem: The number of K-automorphisms of L is at most [L:K].
conclude: So the powers of φ are all the automorphisms.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a finite Galois extension E/F, the order of Gal(E/F) equals [E:F].

drafts.proof_strategy: Write E = F(α) and count automorphisms by the roots of the minimal polynomial of α.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The primitive element theorem gives E = F(α).
derive: The minimal polynomial m of α has degree [E:F].
derive: Normality and separability mean that m has [E:F] distinct roots in E.
construct: Each root of m determines exactly one F-automorphism of E.
conclude: Hence |Gal(E/F)| = [E:F].

drafts.proof_strategy: Prove both round trips using that E/K is Galois for intermediate K and Artin's theorem for subgroups.
sketch_steps: setup: For an intermediate field K, E/K is Galois, so its group has order [E:K].
derive: Elements fixed by the fixing subgroup of K lie in K, so the fixed field of Fix(K) equals K.
apply_theorem: For a subgroup H, Artin's theorem gives [E:E^H] = |H|.
derive: The fixing subgroup of E^H contains H and has the same order, so it equals H.
conclude: The two maps are mutually inverse and reverse inclusions.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a finite Galois extension E/F, the fixed field of the fixing subgroup of an intermediate field K is K, and the fixing subgroup of the fixed field of a subgroup H is H.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the fixed field property of Galois extensions and compare orders using Artin's theorem.
sketch_steps: translate: Since E/K is Galois with group Fix(K), its fixed field is K.
apply_theorem: Artin's theorem gives [E:E^H] = |H|.
derive: The extension E/E^H is Galois, so |Fix(E^H)| = [E:E^H].
conclude: Since H is contained in Fix(E^H) and the orders agree, they are equal.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a finite Galois extension E/F, an element x of E is fixed by every element of Gal(E/F) if and only if x lies in F.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="galois_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="galois_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="automorphism_apply"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: The conjugates of x are the images under the group, and a fixed x has only itself as conjugate.
sketch_steps: derive: If x is in F then every F-automorphism fixes it.
setup: Conversely let m be the minimal polynomial of a fixed element x.
derive: Each root of m is an image σ(x), which equals x by assumption.
derive: Separability means that m has simple roots, so deg m = 1.
conclude: Hence x lies in F.

drafts.canonical_statement: If a finite group G acts faithfully on a field E by field automorphisms, then E over the fixed field E^G is Galois and [E:E^G] = |G|.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="field_group_action"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="galois_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fixed_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ext_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fixed_field"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="size"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use orbit polynomials to bound the degree above and Dedekind independence of automorphisms to bound it below.
sketch_steps: construct: For x in E, the product of X - y over the orbit of x is G-invariant.
derive: That polynomial is separable and splits in E, so E/E^G is separable and normal.
derive: Every element has degree at most |G| over E^G, so the primitive element argument gives [E:E^G] ≤ |G|.
apply_theorem: Dedekind's lemma on independence of automorphisms gives |G| ≤ [E:E^G].
conclude: Hence [E:E^G] = |G| and the extension is Galois.

drafts.canonical_statement: If E/F is normal and x, y in E have the same minimal polynomial over F, then some F-automorphism σ of E satisfies σ(x) = y.

drafts.proof_strategy: Extend the isomorphism F(x) ≅ F(y) to an embedding into an algebraic closure and use normality to stay inside E.
sketch_steps: construct: Equal minimal polynomials give an F-isomorphism F(x) → F(y) with x ↦ y.
apply_theorem: Extend it to an embedding σ of E into an algebraic closure.
derive: Normality places all conjugates of elements of E inside E, so σ(E) ⊂ E.
derive: An algebraic F-endomorphism of E is surjective.
conclude: So σ is an F-automorphism of E with σ(x) = y.

drafts.canonical_statement: A splitting field of a separable polynomial over F is a Galois extension of F.

drafts.proof_strategy: Combine normality of splitting fields with separability of the generators.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: A splitting field is a finite normal extension.
derive: Each root a_i of f has a minimal polynomial dividing f, so it is separable over F.
apply_theorem: An extension generated by separable elements is separable.
conclude: Thus E/F is normal and separable, hence Galois.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a finite Galois extension E/F, if an intermediate field K is Galois over F then its fixing subgroup is normal; conversely for a normal subgroup H, the fixed field E^H is Galois over F and Gal(E^H/F) ≅ Gal(E/F)/H.

drafts.proof_strategy: Conjugation transports fixed fields and fixing subgroups, then the restriction map gives the quotient isomorphism.
sketch_steps: derive: For σ in the group, the fixing subgroup of σ(K) is the conjugate of the fixing subgroup of K.
translate: K/F is normal exactly when K is stable under all σ.
derive: For normal H, the fixed field E^H is stable under σ, so E^H/F is normal and separable.
construct: Restriction gives a homomorphism Gal(E/F) → Gal(E^H/F) with kernel H.
apply_theorem: Restriction is surjective by the extension theorem, and the isomorphism theorem concludes.

drafts.canonical_statement: Over a nontrivial commutative ring R, for a positive integer n, X^n - 1 is the product of Φ_d over the divisors d of n, and Φ_n has degree φ(n).
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="nontrivial_ring"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="gt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_x_pow_sub"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>1</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="product_over_divisors"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="fns1" name="lambda"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="cyclotomic_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="cyclotomic_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="euler_phi"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Group the n-th roots of unity by their exact order, then transfer the integer identity to any ring.
sketch_steps: translate: Over the complex numbers, Φ_d is the product of X - α over primitive d-th roots α.
derive: Each n-th root of unity is a primitive d-th root for exactly one divisor d of n.
derive: Therefore X^n - 1 is the product of Φ_d, and deg Φ_n = φ(n).
conclude: Monic integer coefficients transfer both facts to any nontrivial commutative ring.

drafts.canonical_statement: If n is nonzero in a field F, then μ in F is a root of Φ_n if and only if μ is a primitive n-th root of unity.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the divisor product and the separability of X^n - 1 when n is invertible in F.
sketch_steps: derive: A primitive n-th root is a root of Φ_n by the factorization of X^n - 1 in F.
setup: Conversely suppose Φ_n(μ) = 0 and let d be the order of μ.
derive: The divisor product gives μ^n = 1, so d divides n.
contradiction: If d < n then μ is a double root of X^n - 1, contradicting coprimality with its derivative.
conclude: Therefore d = n.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a positive integer n, Φ_n is irreducible over Q, and it is the minimal polynomial over Q of any primitive n-th root of unity in a field of characteristic zero.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="gt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="cyclotomic_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="field_characteristic"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="primitive_root_of_unity"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="cyclotomic_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimal_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show that the minimal polynomial is stable under μ ↦ μ^p by reduction mod p, and conclude that it contains all primitive roots.
sketch_steps: translate: By Gauss's lemma, the minimal polynomial f of μ has integer coefficients and divides Φ_n.
setup: Fix a prime p not dividing n and write Φ_n = f g over the integers.
contradiction: If g(μ^p) = 0 then f divides g(X^p), and reducing mod p gives a common factor of f and g.
derive: That would give a repeated root of X^n - 1 mod p, which is impossible.
derive: Every primitive n-th root is obtained from μ by such prime powers.
conclude: Hence f = Φ_n, and Φ_n is irreducible.

drafts.canonical_statement: If L is the n-th cyclotomic extension of Q with n ≥ 1, then L/Q is Galois, [L:Q] = φ(n), and Gal(L/Q) is isomorphic to (Z/nZ)^×.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="gt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="cyclotomic_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="galois_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ext_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="euler_phi"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="isomorphic_groups"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="galois_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="zmod_units"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use the irreducibility of Φ_n for the degree and the action on ζ for an injection into (Z/nZ)^×.
sketch_steps: translate: L = Q(ζ) is the splitting field of the separable polynomial X^n - 1, so L/Q is Galois.
apply_theorem: Irreducibility of Φ_n gives [L:Q] = φ(n).
construct: Define a(σ) by σ(ζ) = ζ^a(σ), which is an injective homomorphism into (Z/nZ)^×.
conclude: Comparing orders shows that it is an isomorphism.

drafts.canonical_statement: Main step of the Abel-Ruffini theorem, one direction of the Galois solvability criterion: if an irreducible polynomial q over F has a root solvable by radicals, then the Galois group of q is solvable.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="field_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="solvable_by_radicals"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="irreducible_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_eval"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="solvable_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_galois_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Induct on the construction of x, using solvability of Gal(X^n - a) and closure of solvable groups under extensions and quotients.
sketch_steps: induction: Induct on how x is obtained by field operations and radicals from F.
derive: The group of X^n - 1 is abelian, and over its splitting field the group of X^n - a is abelian too.
apply_theorem: Solvable groups are closed under subgroups, quotients and extensions.
derive: So the minimal polynomial of x has a solvable Galois group.
conclude: Since q is a scalar multiple of that polynomial, its Galois group is solvable.

drafts.canonical_statement: For a field F, the Galois group of X^n - a over F is solvable.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="solvable_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_galois_group"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_x_pow_sub"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Split into the cyclotomic step and the radical step, each abelian, and combine using extensions of solvable groups.
sketch_steps: case_split: The cases a = 0 and n = 0 give a trivial group.
derive: The group of X^n - 1 embeds in the unit group of integers modulo the order, hence is abelian.
derive: Over the field containing the roots of unity, σ ↦ σ(b)/b embeds the group of X^n - a in an abelian group.
apply_theorem: Extensions of solvable groups are solvable.
conclude: So the group of X^n - a is solvable.

drafts.canonical_statement: Fundamental theorem of algebra: every nonconstant complex polynomial has a complex root; equivalently, C is algebraically closed.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="polynomial_over"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="C"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="gt"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="C"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_eval"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="algebraically_closed"></n1:OMS><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="C"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Combine the intermediate value theorem and quadratic roots with Sylow theory on a Galois closure over R.
sketch_steps: derive: Odd-degree real polynomials have a real root, so R has no nontrivial odd-degree extension.
derive: Every complex number has a square root, so C has no quadratic extension.
construct: Take a finite extension L of C that is Galois over R, with group G.
apply_theorem: The fixed field of a Sylow 2-subgroup has odd degree over R, hence G is a 2-group.
contradiction: A nontrivial Gal(L/C) has an index 2 subgroup, whose fixed field is a quadratic extension of C.
conclude: Hence L = C, and C is algebraically closed.

drafts.canonical_statement: If [E:F] = 2^n, then the degree over F of every element of E is a power of 2.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ext_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="exists"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="poly_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimal_polynomial"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Use that the degree divides [E:F] and classify the divisors of a prime power.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: The degree of the minimal polynomial divides [E:F] = 2^n.
conclude: Divisors of 2^n are exactly 2^k with k ≤ n.

drafts.canonical_statement: A degree 2^n extension E of Q contains no element whose cube is 2; this is the algebraic core of the impossibility of doubling the cube.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="finite_extension"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="ext_degree"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMS cd="setname1" name="Q"></n1:OMS></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="neq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="power"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>3</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Show X^3 - 2 is the minimal polynomial and use that 3 does not divide 2^n.
sketch_steps: setup: Suppose α in E satisfies α^3 = 2.
derive: The rational root test shows that 2 is not a rational cube, so X^3 - 2 is irreducible over Q.
derive: Thus the minimal polynomial of α has degree 3.
apply_theorem: The degree of α divides [E:Q] = 2^n.
contradiction: The prime 3 does not divide a power of 2.

drafts.canonical_statement: (Two-variable form; the n-variable form is a separate card.) For nonnegative reals a and b, sqrt(ab) ≤ (a+b)/2.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="root"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="times"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="divide"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>2</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Compare squares of the two nonnegative sides and use (a-b)^2 ≥ 0.
sketch_steps: setup: Note that (a+b)/2 is nonnegative.
derive: Expand ((a+b)/2)^2 - ab = (a-b)^2/4 ≥ 0.
conclude: Taking square roots gives sqrt(ab) ≤ (a+b)/2.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the weighted AM-GM inequality with all weights equal to 1/n, then rewrite the product of powers.
sketch_steps: setup: Take the weights w_i = 1/n, which are nonnegative and sum to 1.
apply_theorem: The weighted AM-GM inequality gives ∏ z_i^(1/n) ≤ Σ z_i/n.
translate: Since z_i ≥ 0, ∏ z_i^(1/n) equals (∏ z_i)^(1/n).
conclude: Factor 1/n out of the sum to obtain the claimed bound.

sketch_steps: derive: Expand to get (a^2+b^2)(c^2+d^2) - (ac+bd)^2 = (ad-bc)^2.
conclude: The square is nonnegative, so the inequality holds.

sketch_steps: setup: Put A = Σ f(i)^2, B = Σ f(i)g(i), C = Σ g(i)^2.
derive: For all real t, A t^2 + 2 B t + C = Σ (t f(i) + g(i))^2 ≥ 0.
case_split: If A = 0, every f(i) vanishes and B = 0.
conclude: If A > 0, the discriminant is nonpositive, so B^2 ≤ AC.

sketch_steps: setup: Put A = (Σ f(i)^p)^(1/p) and B = (Σ g(i)^q)^(1/q).
case_split: If A = 0 or B = 0, one of the functions vanishes and both sides are 0.
apply_theorem: Otherwise apply Young's inequality to f(i)/A and g(i)/B.
derive: Summing over i bounds Σ f(i)g(i)/(AB) by 1/p + 1/q = 1.
conclude: Multiply by AB.

drafts.proof_strategy: Split (f+g)^p into two products and apply Hölder's inequality to each.
sketch_steps: case_split: The case p = 1 is an equality, so assume p > 1 and let q be the conjugate exponent.
translate: Write (f+g)^p = f (f+g)^(p-1) + g (f+g)^(p-1).
apply_theorem: Apply Hölder to both sums, using (p-1)q = p.
derive: Obtain Σ (f+g)^p ≤ (‖f‖_p + ‖g‖_p) (Σ (f+g)^p)^(1/q).
conclude: Divide by (Σ (f+g)^p)^(1/q) when it is positive; otherwise the claim is trivial.

sketch_steps: case_split: If a = 0 or b = 0, the left side is 0 and the right side is nonnegative.
apply_theorem: Otherwise use weighted AM-GM with weights 1/p and 1/q on a^p and b^q.
derive: The geometric mean simplifies to ab.
conclude: Hence ab ≤ a^p/p + b^q/q.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use the tangent line lower bound of a convex function at x, evaluated at the root r.
sketch_steps: derive: Since f(x) ≥ 0 and d > 0, f(x)/d ≥ 0, so x' ≤ x.
case_split: Compare r and x using the slope inequalities of a convex function.
derive: In each case f(x) + d(r-x) ≤ f(r) = 0.
conclude: Dividing by d gives r ≤ x - f(x)/d.

drafts.proof_strategy: Rewrite the error as an integral of f(x)-f(a) and bound the integrand by L(x-a).
sketch_steps: translate: Write the error as ∫_a^b (f(x) - f(a)) dx.
derive: Bound the absolute value of the integral by the integral of the absolute value.
apply_theorem: Use |f(x) - f(a)| ≤ L(x-a) and monotonicity of the integral.
conclude: Compute ∫_a^b L(x-a) dx = L(b-a)^2/2.

drafts.canonical_statement: The intersection of an arbitrary family of convex subsets of a real vector space is convex.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="real_vector_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="convex_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="convex_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="set_family_inter"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Check the convex combination inside each member of the family.
sketch_steps: setup: Take x,y in the intersection and weights a,b ≥ 0 with a+b = 1.
derive: For each member s, convexity of s gives ax+by in s.
conclude: So ax+by lies in the intersection.

drafts.canonical_statement: If f is convex on S, then for every real r the sublevel set {x in S | f(x) ≤ r} is convex.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="real_vector_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="convex_function_on"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="convex_set"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="sublevel_set_on"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Bound f at a convex combination by the convexity inequality and the two sublevel bounds.
sketch_steps: setup: Take x,y in the sublevel set and weights a,b ≥ 0 with a+b = 1.
derive: Convexity of S puts ax+by in S.
derive: Convexity of f gives f(ax+by) ≤ a f(x) + b f(y) ≤ r.
conclude: So ax+by is in the sublevel set.

drafts.canonical_statement: If f is convex on S and a in S is a local minimizer of f on S, then a is a global minimizer of f on S.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normed_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="convex_function_on"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="local_minimizer_on"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimizer_on"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Move along the segment from a to x and combine local minimality with the convexity inequality.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix x in S and consider points a + t(x-a) for small t in (0,1).
apply_theorem: Local minimality gives f(a) ≤ f(a + t(x-a)) for small t.
derive: Convexity gives f(a + t(x-a)) ≤ (1-t) f(a) + t f(x).
conclude: Rearranging and dividing by t gives f(a) ≤ f(x).

drafts.canonical_statement: If f is strictly convex on S, then f has at most one minimizer on S.

drafts.proof_strategy: Test the midpoint of two distinct minimizers against strict convexity.
sketch_steps: contradiction: Suppose x ≠ y are both minimizers on S.
derive: Minimality of both points gives f(x) = f(y).
derive: The midpoint lies in S and strict convexity gives a smaller value there.
conclude: This contradicts minimality, hence x = y.

drafts.canonical_statement: If f is convex on S and has Fréchet derivative L at a in S, then f(a) + L(x-a) ≤ f(x) for all x in S.

drafts.proof_strategy: Bound the difference quotient along the segment from a to x by convexity and pass to the limit.
sketch_steps: derive: For t in (0,1), convexity gives f(a + t(x-a)) ≤ (1-t) f(a) + t f(x).
translate: Rearrange to (f(a + t(x-a)) - f(a))/t ≤ f(x) - f(a).
apply_theorem: By the chain rule the quotient tends to L(x-a) as t tends to 0 from the right.
conclude: Passing to the limit gives L(x-a) ≤ f(x) - f(a).

drafts.canonical_statement: If f is convex on S and has Fréchet derivative L at a in S, then a minimizes f on S if and only if L(x-a) ≥ 0 for all x in S.
drafts.openmath_xml: <n1:OMOBJ xmlns:n1="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="and"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="normed_space"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v1"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="convex_function_on"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="has_frechet_derivative_at"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="equivalent"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="minimizer_on"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v3"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMBIND><n1:OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"></n1:OMS><n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV></n1:OMBVAR><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="set1" name="in"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v2"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="relation1" name="geq"></n1:OMS><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="pals2" cdbase="urn:pals:openmath:cd:v1" name="fn_value"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v4"></n1:OMV><n1:OMA><n1:OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"></n1:OMS><n1:OMV name="v6"></n1:OMV><n1:OMV name="v5"></n1:OMV></n1:OMA></n1:OMA><n1:OMI>0</n1:OMI></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMA></n1:OMA></n1:OMBIND></n1:OMOBJ>
drafts.proof_strategy: Take one-sided difference quotients along segments from a; minimality gives one direction and convexity gives the other.
sketch_steps: setup: By the chain rule the quotient (f(a + t(x-a)) - f(a))/t tends to L(x-a) as t tends to 0 from the right.
derive: If a is a minimizer, the quotient is nonnegative for t in (0,1), so L(x-a) ≥ 0.
derive: Convexity bounds the quotient above by f(x) - f(a), so L(x-a) ≤ f(x) - f(a).
conclude: If L(x-a) ≥ 0 on S, then f(a) ≤ f(x) for all x in S.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a real locally convex topological vector space, if x is not in the closed convex set t, there are a continuous linear functional f and a real u with f(x) < u and u < f(b) for all b in t.

drafts.proof_strategy: Thicken the closed convex set by a convex neighbourhood, then separate using the Minkowski functional and the analytic Hahn-Banach theorem.
sketch_steps: setup: Choose a convex open neighbourhood V of 0 with x + V disjoint from t.
apply_theorem: The Minkowski functional and analytic Hahn-Banach give a continuous linear f and c with f < c on x + V and c ≤ f on t.
derive: Since x is in x + V, f(x) < c.
conclude: Take u = (f(x) + c)/2, so f(x) < u < f(b) for all b in t.

drafts.canonical_statement: If s is contained in a convex set t, then the convex hull of s is contained in t.

drafts.proof_strategy: Use that the convex hull is the intersection of all convex supersets.
sketch_steps: translate: conv(s) is the intersection of all convex sets containing s.
conclude: t is one of those sets, so conv(s) ⊆ t.

drafts.canonical_statement: In a d-dimensional real vector space, every point x of the convex hull of s lies in the convex hull of a finite subset of s with at most d+1 points.

drafts.proof_strategy: Take a representation with the minimal number of points and show those points are affinely independent.
sketch_steps: setup: Write x as a convex combination of finitely many points of s with the fewest possible points.
contradiction: If the points are affinely dependent, shift the coefficients along a dependency.
derive: Some coefficient becomes zero while the others stay nonnegative, reducing the number of points.
derive: So the points are affinely independent.
conclude: Affine independence bounds their number by dim E + 1.

drafts.canonical_statement: A compact convex subset s of a Hausdorff real locally convex topological vector space equals the closure of the convex hull of its extreme points.

drafts.proof_strategy: First obtain extreme points by Zorn and separation, then separate any missing point using Hahn-Banach.
sketch_steps: apply_theorem: Zorn's lemma gives a minimal closed extreme subset of a nonempty compact set.
derive: Separation shows the minimal extreme subset is a single point, so extreme points exist.
translate: The closure of the convex hull of the extreme points is a closed convex subset of s.
contradiction: A point of s outside it would be separated by a continuous linear functional.
derive: The face where that functional attains its extremum contains an extreme point on the wrong side.
conclude: Hence the closure of the convex hull of the extreme points equals s.

sketch_steps: construct: Pick x_0 and set x_(n+1) = f(x_n).
derive: d(x_(n+1), x_n) ≤ K^n d(x_1, x_0), so the sequence is Cauchy.
apply_theorem: Completeness gives a limit x.
derive: Continuity of f gives f(x) = x.
conclude: Two fixed points satisfy d(x,y) ≤ K d(x,y), forcing x = y.

derive: Therefore d(x_0, a) ≤ d(x_0, f(x_0))/(1-K).

derive: P has degree less than n.

conclude: Hence the interpolating polynomial is unique.

conclude: Periodicity gives e^(2π(m-n)i) = 1, so the integral vanishes.

drafts.proof_strategy: Apply the product-to-sum formula and integrate cos(kx) for nonzero integer k.
sketch_steps: translate: cos(mx)cos(nx) = (cos((m-n)x) + cos((m+n)x))/2.
derive: Both m-n and m+n are nonzero integers since m ≠ n.
derive: For an integer k ≠ 0, the integral of cos(kx) over [-π,π] is (sin(kπ) - sin(-kπ))/k = 0.
conclude: Adding the two integrals gives 0.

drafts.proof_strategy: Compute the normalized inner product of two modes as the integral of a single exponential.
sketch_steps: translate: The inner product of modes m and n is the normalized integral of e^(2πi(n-m)x/T).
case_split: For m = n the integrand is 1 and the total mass is 1.
derive: For m ≠ n the exponential integrates to 0 over a full period.
conclude: Therefore the family is orthonormal.

sketch_steps: translate: The coefficient is the normalized circle integral of the (-n)-th mode times the lift of f.
derive: The normalized circle integral is 1/(b-a) times the integral over [a,b].
conclude: The (-n)-th mode at x equals e^(-2πinx/(b-a)).

sketch_steps: translate: The coefficient is the integral of the (-n)-th mode times f.
derive: The absolute value of the integral is at most the integral of the absolute value.
conclude: The mode has absolute value 1, leaving the integral of |f|.

sketch_steps: construct: Let y = Σ ⟨v_i,x⟩ v_i over i in s.
derive: x-y is orthogonal to each v_i, hence to y.
apply_theorem: The Pythagorean theorem gives ‖x‖^2 = ‖x-y‖^2 + ‖y‖^2.
conclude: Orthonormality gives ‖y‖^2 = Σ |⟨v_i,x⟩|^2, so the bound follows.

derive: The mode has antiderivative (b-a)/(-2πin) times itself because n ≠ 0.
apply_theorem: Integrate by parts.
derive: Periodicity gives equal mode values at a and b in the boundary term.
conclude: Collect terms into the stated identity.

drafts.proof_strategy: Show the Fourier modes are a Hilbert basis of L^2 of the circle, then use the abstract Parseval identity.
sketch_steps: setup: Lift f to L^2 of the circle of period b-a with normalized measure.
derive: The Fourier modes are orthonormal in L^2.
apply_theorem: Stone-Weierstrass and density of continuous functions give completeness of the modes.
apply_theorem: The abstract Parseval identity gives Σ |⟨e_n,f⟩|^2 = ‖f‖^2.
conclude: Identify ⟨e_n,f⟩ with c_n(f) and ‖f‖^2 with the normalized integral.

drafts.canonical_statement: If f is continuous on the circle of period T and its Fourier coefficients are summable, then the Fourier series Σ c_n(f) e_n(x) converges to f(x) at every point x.

drafts.proof_strategy: The series converges uniformly by the M-test and its uniform limit agrees with the L^2 limit f.
sketch_steps: derive: Since |e_n| = 1 and the coefficients are summable, the series converges uniformly to a continuous g.
apply_theorem: The Fourier series of f converges to f in L^2.
derive: Uniform convergence implies L^2 convergence, so g = f almost everywhere.
derive: Both functions are continuous, so g = f everywhere.
conclude: Hence the series converges to f(x) at every x.

drafts.canonical_statement: For an integrable f on ℝ, the integral of e^(-2πivw) f(v) dv tends to 0 as |w| tends to infinity.

drafts.proof_strategy: Reduce to continuous compactly supported functions by density and use a half-period shift.
sketch_steps: translate: The integral is bounded by ‖f‖_1, so by density assume f is continuous with compact support.
derive: Shifting v by 1/(2w) flips the sign of the exponential.
derive: So the integral is half of the integral of the exponential times f(v) - f(v + 1/(2w)).
apply_theorem: Uniform continuity of f makes this difference small as |w| grows.
conclude: Hence the integral tends to 0.
